Test Scenario: Successful login with valid MFA
Test Case Description: Verify that a registered user can successfully log in with valid credentials and MFA and is redirected to the dashboard within 3 seconds.
Preconditions: User is on the login page and has a valid username/password and registered MFA device.
Test Steps:
1. Enter valid username.
2. Enter valid password.
3. Submit credentials.
4. Enter valid OTP/MFA code.
5. Submit MFA code.
Test Data: username: validUser, password: SecurePass123!, otp: 123456
Expected Result: User is authenticated, redirected to the dashboard, and login completes within 3 seconds.

Test Scenario: Account lockout after 5 failed password attempts
Test Case Description: Verify that the system locks the account for 15 minutes and sends an email alert after 5 consecutive invalid password attempts.
Preconditions: User is a registered user with MFA enabled.
Test Steps:
1. Enter valid username.
2. Enter invalid password.
3. Repeat steps 1-2 for 5 consecutive attempts.
4. Observe system response.
Test Data: username: validUser, password: WrongPass1; WrongPass2; WrongPass3; WrongPass4; WrongPass5
Expected Result: Account is locked, login is denied, a lockout message is displayed, and an email alert is triggered to the registered email.

Test Scenario: MFA required on unrecognized device
Test Case Description: Verify that MFA challenge is triggered when a login is attempted from a new or unrecognized device, even with valid credentials.
Preconditions: User has valid credentials and MFA enabled; login attempt originates from a new/unrecognized browser or device.
Test Steps:
1. Open login page from a new/unrecognized device/browser.
2. Enter valid username and password.
3. Submit credentials.
4. Verify additional authentication step.
Test Data: username: validUser, password: SecurePass123!, device: newDevice
Expected Result: System prompts for MFA challenge before granting access; access is granted only after valid MFA submission.

Test Scenario: Login page UI validation and error messaging
Test Case Description: Verify that login validation messages are displayed properly for empty username/password and invalid credentials.
Preconditions: User is on the login page.
Test Steps:
1. Leave username empty and enter valid password.
2. Submit login.
3. Enter username and leave password empty.
4. Submit login.
5. Enter invalid username/password.
6. Submit login.
Test Data: username: , password: SecurePass123!; username: validUser, password: ; username: wrongUser, password: wrongPass
Expected Result: Appropriate validation messages appear for empty fields and invalid credentials; error messages are visible and accessible.

Test Scenario: Real-time NAV and P&L update within latency SLA
Test Case Description: Verify that NAV and position-level P&L values update with market data no older than 15 seconds when the dashboard loads.
Preconditions: Investment manager is logged into the portfolio dashboard and market data feed is active.
Test Steps: 1. Load the portfolio dashboard.\n2. Compare timestamps of NAV and P&L values with current time.\n3. Verify update latency.
Test Data: Market data delay: 12 seconds
Expected Result: Displayed NAV/P&L values are based on market data no older than 15 seconds from current time.

Test Scenario: Automatic refresh after trade settlement
Test Case Description: Verify that portfolio value updates automatically after a pending trade settles without requiring a manual page refresh.
Preconditions: A pending trade exists and the dashboard is open.
Test Steps: 1. Identify a pending trade on the dashboard.\n2. Simulate trade settlement.\n3. Observe dashboard without refresh.
Test Data: Trade status changes from PENDING to SETTLED
Expected Result: Portfolio value updates automatically and the dashboard reflects the settled trade immediately.

Test Scenario: Staleness warning during market data feed outage
Test Case Description: Verify that a clear staleness warning indicator and last successful feed timestamp appear when the market data feed is unavailable for more than 30 seconds.
Preconditions: Portfolio dashboard is open and market data feed outage is simulated for >30 seconds.
Test Steps: 1. Simulate market data feed outage for 31 seconds.\n2. Observe dashboard warnings.\n3. Verify displayed timestamp.
Test Data: Outage duration: 31 seconds
Expected Result: System displays a staleness warning indicator with the timestamp of the last successful feed.

Test Scenario: Submit compliant Limit order successfully
Test Case Description: Verify that a trader can submit a Limit order for an approved security when pre-trade compliance checks pass and receive an Order ID within 2 seconds.
Preconditions: Trader is logged in, security is approved, and pre-trade compliance is satisfied.
Test Steps:
1. Open order entry.
2. Select Limit order type and approved security.
3. Enter valid order quantity and price.
4. Submit order.
Test Data: Order type: Limit, Security: approvedStock, Quantity: 100, Price: 25.50
Expected Result: Order is routed to OMS, confirmation appears with Order ID, and response completes within 2 seconds.

Test Scenario: Reject order breaching position limit rule
Test Case Description: Verify that an order breaching position limit is rejected with a descriptive breach message and logged in the audit trail.
Preconditions: Trader is logged in and order exceeds configured position limit.
Test Steps:
1. Open order entry.
2. Enter order details exceeding the position limit.
3. Submit order.
4. Verify rejection message.
5. Check audit log entry.
Test Data: Order quantity or value exceeds position limit for the trader
Expected Result: Order is rejected with a clear breach message; rejection is recorded in audit logs.

Test Scenario: Cancel pending order and update blotter in real time
Test Case Description: Verify that canceling a PENDING order sends a cancellation request, updates status to CANCELLED, and reflects the change in the blotter immediately.
Preconditions: Trader has a PENDING order visible in the order blotter.
Test Steps:
1. Locate a PENDING order.
2. Click Cancel Order.
3. Confirm cancellation.
4. Verify order status and blotter update.
Test Data: Order status: PENDING
Expected Result: Order status updates to CANCELLED and blotter reflects cancellation in real time.

Test Scenario: Generate scheduled SEC 13F report successfully
Test Case Description: Verify that the scheduled SEC 13F report generates, saves to the repository, and sends email notification at end of quarter.
Preconditions: Report schedule is active at end of quarter and system has valid portfolio data.
Test Steps: 1. Trigger scheduled 13F report run.\n2. Verify report generation completion.\n3. Validate report location and notification.
Test Data: Portfolio size: <=10,000 positions
Expected Result: Compliant 13F report is generated, saved to designated repository, and compliance team receives email notification.

Test Scenario: Ad-hoc AIFMD report completes within 10 minutes
Test Case Description: Verify that ad-hoc AIFMD Annex IV report generation for a fund with up to 10,000 positions completes within 10 minutes and is available in XML and PDF.
Preconditions: Compliance officer triggers ad-hoc report and the fund has <=10,000 positions.
Test Steps: 1. Trigger ad-hoc AIFMD report.\n2. Monitor generation time.\n3. Verify XML and PDF availability.
Test Data: Position count: 9,850
Expected Result: Report generation completes within 10 minutes and both XML and PDF files are available for download.

Test Scenario: Handle corrupt position data during report generation
Test Case Description: Verify that a report job fails gracefully on corrupt data, logs field-level errors, and notifies compliance team via email.
Preconditions: Report generation is initiated with missing or corrupt position data.
Test Steps: 1. Trigger report generation with corrupt position data.\n2. Observe job failure handling.\n3. Validate error log and notification.
Test Data: Corrupt/missing position data in source feed
Expected Result: Job fails gracefully, creates an error log with field-level detail, and sends email notification to the compliance team.

Test Scenario: Successful ingestion of daily custodian file and reconciliation
Test Case Description: Verify that a valid custodian file is ingested and reconciled against internal records by 07:00 AM EST with breaks flagged in the reconciliation dashboard.
Preconditions: Valid SWIFT MT535 file is available by 05:30 AM EST.
Test Steps: 1. Provide valid custodian file by 05:30 AM EST.\n2. Execute ingestion pipeline.\n3. Verify reconciliation completion and dashboard breaks.
Test Data: File type: SWIFT MT535, arrival time: 05:30 AM EST
Expected Result: All records are loaded and reconciled; any breaks are flagged in the reconciliation dashboard by 07:00 AM EST.

Test Scenario: Quarantine malformed custodian file and alert ops
Test Case Description: Verify that a malformed or schema-invalid custodian file is quarantined, processing halts for that source, an alert is raised, and prior day data remains unchanged.
Preconditions: Malformed custodian file is received by the ingestion pipeline.
Test Steps: 1. Provide malformed custodian file.\n2. Run ingestion pipeline.\n3. Verify quarantine action, alert, and data integrity.
Test Data: Malformed SWIFT MT535 or CSV file
Expected Result: File is quarantined, processing stops for that source, operations receives an alert, and previous day data remains unchanged.

Test Scenario: Retry pipeline failures with exponential backoff and escalate
Test Case Description: Verify that an infrastructure failure triggers up to 3 automatic retries with exponential backoff before escalating to PagerDuty with full error context.
Preconditions: Infrastructure failure occurs during data ingestion.
Test Steps: 1. Simulate infrastructure failure.\n2. Observe retry behavior.\n3. Validate escalation after retries.
Test Data: Failure condition: temporary infrastructure outage
Expected Result: System retries ingestion up to 3 times with exponential backoff; if still failing, it escalates to PagerDuty with full error context.

Test Scenario: Deny access to Compliance Reports for Trader role
Test Case Description: Verify that a Trader is denied access to the Compliance Reports module, sees a permission error, and the attempt is logged in the audit trail.
Preconditions: User is logged in as Trader.
Test Steps:
1. Login as Trader.
2. Navigate to Compliance Reports module.
3. Attempt access.
4. Check audit log entry.
Test Data: Role: Trader
Expected Result: Access is denied, permission error message is displayed, and the attempt is recorded in the audit trail.

Test Scenario: Create custom role and apply permissions within 60 seconds
Test Case Description: Verify that an administrator can create a custom role, assign permissions, save it, and have the role available for assignment and enforcement within 60 seconds while logging the change.
Preconditions: Administrator is logged into role management and custom role permissions are defined.
Test Steps:
1. Open role creation UI.
2. Define custom role and assign permissions.
3. Save role.
4. Verify role availability and audit log entry.
5. Assign role to a user and validate permissions.
Test Data: Role name: RiskAnalyst, Permissions: view reports, export data
Expected Result: Custom role is available for assignment within 60 seconds, permissions take effect, and the change is captured in the audit log.

Test Scenario: Invalidate session after role change
Test Case Description: Verify that changing a user's role from Trader to Read-Only invalidates the active session within 5 minutes and new permissions apply on next login.
Preconditions: User has an active session as Trader; admin changes role to Read-Only.
Test Steps:
1. Have Trader user logged in.
2. Admin changes role to Read-Only.
3. Wait up to 5 minutes.
4. Attempt action requiring Trader permissions.
5. Re-login and verify new permissions.
Test Data: Original role: Trader, New role: Read-Only
Expected Result: Active session is invalidated within 5 minutes; user is prompted to re-login and the new Read-Only permissions apply after login.

Test Scenario: Maintain 95th percentile page load and API response SLAs under 200 users
Test Case Description: Verify that under 200 concurrent users during peak hours, 95% of page loads complete in ≤2 seconds and 95% of API responses complete in ≤500ms with zero errors.
Preconditions: Performance test environment simulates 200 concurrent users during peak market hours.
Test Steps: 1. Simulate 200 concurrent users accessing dashboard workflows.\n2. Measure page load times and API response times.\n3. Verify error rate.
Test Data: Concurrent users: 200, Peak hour traffic pattern
Expected Result: 95% of page loads are ≤2 seconds, 95% of API responses are ≤500ms, and error rate remains at 0%.

Test Scenario: Graceful degradation above 200 concurrent users
Test Case Description: Verify that with 300 concurrent users, core trading functions remain available, the system queues requests or throttles gracefully, and an ops alert is triggered without crashing.
Preconditions: Load test environment simulates 300 concurrent users.
Test Steps: 1. Simulate 300 concurrent users.\n2. Execute core trading workflows.\n3. Observe system behavior and alerts.
Test Data: Concurrent users: 300
Expected Result: System degrades gracefully, core trading functions remain available, queueing/throttling occurs, and ops alert is triggered.

Test Scenario: Create immutable audit log entry for user actions
Test Case Description: Verify that all user actions generate an immutable audit log entry within 1 second containing required fields and are retained correctly.
Preconditions: User performs actions such as login, order submit, report export, or config change.
Test Steps: 1. Perform a user action.\n2. Check audit log entry.\n3. Confirm required fields and timestamp.
Test Data: Action: login, User ID: testUser, IP address: 10.0.0.1
Expected Result: Audit log entry is created within 1 second and includes User ID, UTC timestamp, action type, affected entity, IP address, and outcome.

Test Scenario: Audit log search returns results within 5 seconds
Test Case Description: Verify that a compliance officer querying audit logs for a user's activity over a date range receives results within 5 seconds.
Preconditions: Compliance officer is logged into audit log query interface.
Test Steps: 1. Enter user ID and date range.\n2. Execute search.\n3. Measure response time.
Test Data: User ID: testUser, Date range: 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-15
Expected Result: Audit search returns complete results within 5 seconds containing all actions in the specified period.

Test Scenario: Block audit log modification or deletion attempts
Test Case Description: Verify that any attempt to modify or delete an audit log entry is rejected, itself logged as a security event, and alerts are sent to the CISO team.
Preconditions: User (including admin) attempts to modify or delete an audit log entry.
Test Steps: 1. Attempt to modify or delete an audit log entry.\n2. Observe system response.\n3. Verify security event log and alert.
Test Data: Attempt type: modify or delete audit log entry
Expected Result: Modification or deletion is rejected; attempt is logged as a security event and a CISO alert is generated.
